questions.question: Explain how burning coal in power stations leads to acid rain. Include a chemical equation.
questions.expected_answer: Coal contains sulfur, which burns to form sulfur dioxide: S + O2 → SO2. Sulfur dioxide is an acidic non-metal oxide; in the air it reacts with oxygen and water to form sulfuric acid (2SO2 + O2 + 2H2O → 2H2SO4), which falls as acid rain.

questions.question: Describe two effects of acid rain and explain one of them using chemistry.
questions.expected_answer: Any two of: damage to limestone and marble buildings, faster corrosion of metals, nutrient loss and aluminium toxicity in soil, acidified lakes killing fish, lung irritation. E.g. marble is calcium carbonate, a base, which reacts with the acid: CaCO3 + H2SO4 → CaSO4 + H2O + CO2, and the products wash away.

questions.question: Why do farmers spread agricultural lime on acidic soils, and how does it work?
questions.expected_answer: Most crops grow best at pH 6 to 7, and acidic soil reduces nutrient uptake and releases toxic aluminium. Agricultural lime is calcium carbonate, a base, which neutralises the acid in the soil, raising the pH.
